tasks.short: Review books and journal articles for publication.

steps.what: Read books and journal articles submitted for potential publication
Evaluate psychological methods, claims, originality and suitability for publication
Write the publication review with page-specific comments and recommendation
Approve the final publication review, recommendation and editor recipient
Submit the approved publication review to the editor through the peer-review portal

tasks.design: Use a native review template and linked annotations in {DOCS} to reuse page references and required headings. Keep reading, scholarly assessment, substantive review writing and submission through the peer-review-portal category of {OTHER} human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Review notes and page references are copied into the final report.
tasks.enabler_now: Linked annotations and document templates can reduce repeated reference entry.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing originality, research validity and the importance of flaws is expert work.
tasks.human_edge: Give fair criticism and distinguish a fixable limitation from an unsupported central claim.
tasks.altitude: A small reduction in reference copying; scholarly review responsibility is unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: document annotations and native templates can reuse page references while leaving substantive peer-review judgement manual.

assumptions: Boundary includes the manuscript review, written report and editor submission. No model reads confidential manuscripts. Shares are provisional and apply where notes are actually copied into review reports.

The editor supplies manuscript revision, review criteria and submission destination. s1 records comments with page references; s2 supplies the recommendation. s3 reuses those references only; reasoning and substantive prose keep their time.

Test native linked annotations before adding tools. A changed manuscript invalidates page links until checked. s4 approves the complete report and s5 manually submits that exact version; portal automation is not assumed.
No editorial publication decision or response to later author revisions is included. Existing confidentiality terms and reviewer permissions must be checked before configuring note synchronization.
research_questions: Does linked reference reuse save effort without mislocating comments after manuscript revisions?

already_counted.description: Review complete publication report and recommendation

incremental.description: Check annotation compatibility and template changes

approvals.approved_version: Final review text, recommendation, manuscript revision and editor destination approved in s4; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central saves three reference-copying hours less one upkeep. Low assumes annotation reuse already exists, leaving upkeep only. Reading, evaluation, substantive writing and actual submission are unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile specialized bibliographies for outside reading.

steps.what: Find specialized psychology materials and capture their bibliographic metadata
Select specialized materials for relevance, level and student accessibility
Compile bibliographies of specialized materials in the required citation style
Verify final bibliography references and approve the student reading list
Publish the approved specialized bibliography to the student course space

tasks.design: Use the reference-manager and academic-catalogue categories of {OTHER} for metadata import and native citation formatting. The teacher chooses readings, verifies the full bibliography and approves its exact {LMS} publication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bibliographies repeat metadata entry, citation formatting and course-space uploads.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reference imports and citation-style engines perform mechanical compilation.
tasks.still_hard: A correct citation can still be a poor, outdated or inaccessible reading choice.
tasks.human_edge: Choose useful perspectives and an appropriate difficulty level.
tasks.altitude: Less bibliographic formatting; reading selection remains human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: reference managers import catalogue metadata and format citations; selecting suitable materials and checking access remain human work.

assumptions: Boundary includes discovery, selection, formatting, checking and student publication. Shares describe a provisional bibliography task with manual metadata and formatting; already automated lists earn less.

Catalogue publishers supply title, authors, year, identifier, edition and stable record location. s1 imports these and manually enters absent or conflicting metadata in retained time. No model invents titles or identifiers.

s2 records selected identifiers and reading order. s3 uses those records plus teacher-selected citation style; unresolved entries are withheld for manual correction in s4, which verifies edition, identity, links and accessibility.
Test native reference manager and {LMS} bibliography integration first. The final list and cohort are fixed before approval; changed entries invalidate publication approval.
research_questions: How many entries import completely and resolve to the intended accessible edition?

already_counted.description: Verify final entries and student release

incremental.description: Maintain citation styles and broken-link checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact bibliography revision, entry order and course cohort approved in s4; changed entries or audience void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes 15 metadata-entry, 25 citation-formatting and five publication hours less two upkeep. Low assumes metadata and citations already automated, leaving publication only. Selection and final verification retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Look up student organization rules and available institutional resources
Act as adviser to student organizations through discussion of plans and concerns
Draft written follow-up advice and resource links for the student organization
Approve the final student organization advice and representatives receiving it
Send the approved follow-up advice to student organization representatives

tasks.design: Configure a native resource view in {DOCS} and reusable factual link sections in {EMAIL}. The teacher keeps the advisory conversation and case-specific follow-up human, approving the completed message before student delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advisers repeatedly locate rules and copy the same resource links into follow-ups.
tasks.enabler_now: Native saved views and message snippets can reduce lookup and link copying.
tasks.still_hard: Student groups may disagree internally or need sensitive personal support.
tasks.human_edge: Help students make their own decisions while recognizing institutional boundaries.
tasks.altitude: Less resource lookup; relationship and advisory responsibility are unchanged.

reach.task: Connect student groups with educational resources

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: saved institutional resource views and message snippets can reduce repeated lookup and link copying, without replacing student advice.

assumptions: Boundary includes resource lookup, advice and ordinary written follow-up. It does not transfer group governance to the adviser. Shares are provisional and apply to advice that actually has a follow-up.

Institutional resource owners supply approved guidance, revision and contact links. s1 verifies relevance and manually searches exceptions; s2 forms the actual advice in conversation. s3 manually writes case-specific content and selects link snippets.
Test native document views and email snippets first. No conversation recording or automatic interpretation is proposed; s3's retained time includes recalling and expressing the agreed advice.

s4 checks the full message, confidentiality and representative identities. Any edit or changed recipient invalidates s5 approval. Institutional employees are not treated as external, but the student recipients here are outside staff.
research_questions: Are repeated resource lookup and link copying material without counting the advice itself as saved?

already_counted.description: Approve final follow-up and student recipients

incremental.description: Maintain resource links and reusable factual sections

approvals.approved_version: Complete follow-up revision, attachments and representative identities approved in s4; edits require reapproval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes five lookup, three link-copying and five dispatch hours less one upkeep. Low assumes all native aids and sending already efficient, leaving upkeep only. Advisory discussion and tailored advice retain time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Participate in campus and community events.

steps.what: Read campus and community event details and identify the requested participation
Approve the specific event attendance response and any stated participation commitment
Send the approved participation response to the community event organizer
Participate in campus and community events, engaging attendees and responding to questions

tasks.design: Use native invitation details and approved responses in {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}. Reduce repeated detail retrieval and response handling; participation and community interaction retain full time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Event arrangements can repeat date, venue and participation-detail lookup.
tasks.enabler_now: Native calendar invitations keep standard event fields together and can send an approved response.
tasks.still_hard: A useful event contribution depends on live interaction and representing the discipline responsibly.
tasks.human_edge: Connect psychological knowledge to attendees' questions and concerns.
tasks.altitude: Only a small arranging benefit; the event contribution itself is unchanged.

reach.task: Align outreach contributions with educational aims

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: calendar invitations consolidate event details and support attendance responses; this does not reduce substantive participation time.

assumptions: Boundary includes the teacher's small invitation-response component and substantive participation, not event production. Shares are provisional and must not create an administrative baseline where participation is informal and no response occurs.
The organizer supplies event title, date, venue, requested role and reply address. s1 checks omissions manually and reads the substantive programme; native views save only repeated detail navigation.

s2 explicitly composes and checks the final attendance response and any commitment before s3 sends it. For an internal-only organizer, use write_internal instead of act_external. No extra calendar write or attendee-data collection is proposed.
Test existing calendar response configuration first. Where already used or unnecessary, this design has no additional saving; ongoing configuration checking is counted.
research_questions: Is there any repeated arrangement work left after existing calendar use?

already_counted.description: Approve final event response and commitment

approvals.approved_version: Exact response text, participation commitment and organizer address approved in s2; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes two repeated-detail and three dispatch hours less one upkeep. Low assumes native responses already operate or no response is required, leaving upkeep only. Ninety hours of actual participation remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use native reference and communication tools around scholarly and community responsibilities.
role.ambitious_version: Prepare accurate reading resources and clear follow-ups with less copying while retaining personal scholarly and advisory work.
